regional.syndrome: Influenza-like illness with fever, headache, pharyngitis and gastrointestinal symptoms; occasional CNS involvement. High background seroprevalence in central Europe.
regional.headline: European California-serogroup virus causing 'Valtice fever'.
regional.geography: Central and southern Europe, Russia, Central Asia, Africa (Lumbo virus).
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Abrupt fever, profound weakness, myalgia, then vomiting and high-volume diarrhoea with electrolyte derangement, shock and sometimes haemorrhage. Survivors experience uveitis, arthralgia and neurological sequelae; virus persists in semen, aqueous humour and CSF, enabling late sexual transmission and relapse.
regional.headline: Filovirus causing Ebola disease, with case fatality historically 25–90%; now treatable with monoclonal antibodies and preventable by vaccination.
regional.prevention: The rVSV-ZEBOV vaccine (Ervebo) used in ring vaccination, plus the Ad26/MVA regimen; safe burial practices and infection prevention and control.
regional.geography: Central and West Africa — the 2013–2016 West African epidemic caused over 28,000 cases.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: About 80% of infections are asymptomatic; 20% develop West Nile fever; <1% develop neuroinvasive disease — meningitis, encephalitis or a poliomyelitis-like acute flaccid paralysis, with substantial mortality and long-term sequelae in older adults.
regional.headline: Globally the most widespread encephalitic flavivirus, maintained in a bird–mosquito cycle.
regional.prevention: Mosquito control and personal protection; blood-supply nucleic-acid screening; equine vaccines exist but no human vaccine.
regional.geography: Africa, Europe, Middle East, Asia, Australia (Kunjin), and across the Americas since 1999.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Aseptic meningitis or meningoencephalitis, usually self-limiting; also undifferentiated 'summer fever'.
regional.headline: A leading cause of summer aseptic meningitis around the Mediterranean, transmitted by sandflies.

regional.syndrome: Mild influenza-like febrile illness reported in humans; clinical burden poorly quantified.
regional.headline: Widespread Bunyamwera-serogroup virus of Eurasia and Africa; donor of the M segment that created Ngari virus.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.syndrome: Abrupt febrile illness ('Oropouche fever') with severe headache, myalgia, arthralgia, chills, photophobia and nausea; frequently relapsing after a few days of apparent recovery. Aseptic meningitis and meningoencephalitis occur. Vertical transmission with fetal loss and congenital anomalies reported during the 2024 expansion, as well as rare fatalities.
regional.headline: The most important human pathogen of the Simbu serogroup and, after dengue, one of the most frequent arboviral febrile illnesses in the Amazon basin. Major expansion across the Americas from 2023–2024.
regional.prevention: Midge control is difficult (C. paraensis is tiny and bites outdoors by day); fine-mesh screening, repellents, reduction of peridomestic breeding (decaying banana/cacao debris).
regional.geography: Amazon basin — Brazil, Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador, Colombia, Panama, Trinidad; marked 2024 expansion including Cuba and travel-associated cases exported to Europe and North America.
regional.evidence_note: Human infection has been confirmed in this country.

regional.headline: The most geographically widespread tick-borne virus causing human haemorrhagic fever; a WHO priority pathogen requiring high-level containment.
regional.prevention: Tick protection, safe slaughter practice, and strict barrier nursing with full PPE. No licensed vaccine (a Bulgarian inactivated vaccine has limited use).
regional.geography: Africa, the Balkans, Middle East, Central and South Asia, western China; expanding with Hyalomma range into Spain and southern Europe.
regional.evidence_note: Virus, viral RNA or specific antibody found in the reservoir host or in livestock, with no human case reported. The virus is present in the country; whether it has ever infected a person there is unknown.
